name: Eve
role: The first woman, “mother of all the living”
summary: Made from the man's side as a helper suitable for him, she was persuaded by the serpent to eat from the forbidden tree and gave the fruit to her husband. Named Eve because she would be the mother of all the living, she bore Cain, Abel and Seth.
body: The LORD God builds the woman from a rib of the man while he sleeps and brings her to him. He calls her woman, “for out of man she was taken,” and the narrator adds that a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife.

The serpent asks whether God really said they must not eat of any tree, and tells her that they will not die but will be like God, knowing good and evil. She sees that the tree is good for food, pleasing to the eye and desirable for wisdom; she eats and gives to her husband, who is with her. Asked what she has done, she answers, “The serpent deceived me.” Her sentence is pain in childbearing, and her husband will rule over her.

Outside the garden she bears Cain, saying she has brought forth a man with the help of the LORD, and then Abel; after Abel's murder she bears Seth. Paul twice recalls that she was deceived (2 Corinthians 11:3; 1 Timothy 2:13–14).

moments.text: Eats, and gives to her husband
